analysis.title: Morning Market Tidbits: Another fizzy COLA
key_insights: The Social Security cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) will be 3.6% next January, the largest increase since 2023.
BofA estimates the COLA adds $13.5bn to pre-tax income (0.05% of personal income), a modest tailwind to consumer spending.
BofA estimates the COLA adds approximately $145bn to deficits over the next 10 years, all else equal and after accounting for the taxed portion of benefits.

The Social Security Administration pulled its projected trust fund depletion date forward to 2032, owing to changes in the tax treatment of Social Security. Persistent higher inflation could bring it forward further.

Average benefits would drop by about 22% if the trust fund is depleted without Congressional action. Funding the gap with general obligations instead of reform would be another reason for long-end US Treasury yields to press higher.
BofA's 3Q26 GDP tracking estimate is unchanged at 3.7% q/q saar after durable goods and new home sales, against a BofA official GDP forecast of 3.5%.
Today's events are the FOMC rate decision at 14:00 with a press conference at 14:30, wholesale inventories and advance goods trade.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Largest increase since 2023. Adds $13.5bn to pre-tax income, a modest consumer spending tailwind, and about $145bn to 10-year deficits.
Unchanged after durable goods and new home sales. BofA's official 3Q GDP forecast is 3.5%.
Decision due at 14:00 ET on Oct 28 with a press conference at 14:30. The BofA estimate listed in the calendar table is above consensus and the previous level.
Preliminary release due at 8:30 on Oct 28. No BofA estimate or consensus is shown. The 0.5% is the previous reading.

risk_factors: Higher inflation, if it persists, could pull the Social Security trust fund depletion date forward from 2032.
If Congress funds a trust fund shortfall with general obligations instead of reform, long-end US Treasury yields could press higher.
Depletion of the trust fund without Congressional action would cut average benefits by about 22%.
